The paper identifies single-intervention effects from observational and joint-intervention data for specified nonlinear continuous SCMs with additive multivariate Gaussian noise.
Theorem 1 identifies the mean outcome under joint interventions from observational and singleton-intervention distributions for an additive SCM with arbitrary-covariance Gaussian noise.

MIC(G) is a minimum graph-level intervention cover sufficient for every identifiable causal effect in a causal model characterized by G, with do-calculus completeness for computing MIC.
The paper establishes functional central-limit and exchangeable-bootstrap results for regression/counterfactual-distribution operators and related functionals.
